fixes.explanation: Good instinct to look twice, friend, but this one is true. Jesus says, "And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me." (Matthew 18:5). He's pointing to the child He just stood among them (Matthew 18:2), and the welcome doesn't stop at the child. It lands on Jesus Himself. I had to read it twice too.

Good guess, baker, but no servants show up. Jesus says the man will "…go out to search for the one that is lost?" (Matthew 18:12). No delegating, no "can somebody go check on that sheep?" Then Jesus says, "…your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish." (Matthew 18:14). So the story is about how much the Father cares about each one.

No prophet in this verse, baker. Right before this, Jesus talks about two of you agreeing on earth (Matthew 18:19). Then He says, "For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them." (Matthew 18:20). Notice how small that gathering is. Two or three is enough, and no crowd is needed.
